Information since September points to continued labor-market strength and solid real activity, with PCE inflation near the symmetric 2% objective and longer-run expectations stable. The Committee kept the federal funds rate at 2 to 2.25% while signaling that further gradual hikes remain appropriate and continued balance-sheet normalization in Treasuries and agency MBS.

However, SLOOS evidence tempers the otherwise positive tone. Banks tightened lending standards on C&I loans and on construction and land development loans, and tightened other lending terms across borrower sizes; they also reported weaker demand for construction and land development loans. This tightening in credit supply and softer loan demand—particularly in CRE and capex-sensitive segments—aligns with the observed moderation in business fixed investment and implies some headwinds to growth via the credit channel.

Financial stability considerations also lean cautious: elevated asset valuations and high corporate borrowing with weaker leveraged-loan underwriting increase sensitivity to shocks, even as banks remain well capitalized with low funding risks.

Net assessment: underlying growth remains positive with a mildly hawkish policy bias, but SLOOS points to tighter credit conditions and weaker demand in key segments, shifting risks toward balanced-to-slightly-cautious.
